{{Short description|none}}
This is a list of [[formula]]s encountered in [[Riemannian geometry]]. [[Einstein notation]] is used throughout this article. This article uses the "analyst's" [[sign convention]] for Laplacians, except when noted otherwise.

== Christoffel symbols, covariant derivative ==

In a smooth [[coordinate chart]], the [[Christoffel symbols]] of the first kind are given by
: <math>\Gamma_{kij}=\frac12 \left(
        \frac{\partial}{\partial x^j} g_{ki}
        +\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i} g_{kj}
        -\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k} g_{ij}
        \right)
        =\frac12 \left( g_{ki,j} + g_{kj,i} - g_{ij,k} \right) \,,
</math>
and the Christoffel symbols of the second kind by
: <math>\begin{align}
        \Gamma^m{}_{ij} &= g^{mk}\Gamma_{kij}\\
        &=\frac{1}{2}\, g^{mk} \left(
        \frac{\partial}{\partial x^j} g_{ki}
        +\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i} g_{kj}
        -\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k} g_{ij}
        \right)
        =\frac{1}{2}\, g^{mk} \left( g_{ki,j} + g_{kj,i} - g_{ij,k} \right) \,.
        \end{align}
</math>

Here <math>g^{ij}</math> is the [[inverse matrix]] to the metric tensor <math>g_{ij}</math>.  In other words,
: <math>
\delta^i{}_j = g^{ik}g_{kj}
</math>
and thus
: <math>
n = \delta^i{}_i = g^i{}_i = g^{ij}g_{ij}
</math>
is the dimension of the [[manifold]]. Additionally, we can take the trace of contravariant [[tensors]] with respect to <math>g</math> as follows (and similarly for covariant ones): let <math>T</math> be a <math>(2,0)</math> tensor, then its trace with respect to <math>g</math> is 
: <math>
\operatorname{tr}_g T = \operatorname{tr}(v \mapsto g^{-1} T(v,-))
</math> 
where <math>g^{-1}</math> is the isomorphism between the [[cotangent space]] and the tangent space.

Christoffel symbols satisfy the symmetry relations
:<math>\Gamma_{kij} = \Gamma_{kji} </math> or, respectively, <math> \Gamma^i{}_{jk}=\Gamma^i{}_{kj}, </math>
the second of which is equivalent to the torsion-freeness of the [[Levi-Civita connection]].

The contracting relations on the Christoffel symbols are given by
: <math>\Gamma^i{}_{ki}=\frac{1}{2} g^{im}\frac{\partial g_{im}}{\partial x^k}=\frac{1}{2g} \frac{\partial g}{\partial x^k} = \frac{\partial \log \sqrt{|g|}}{\partial x^k} </math>
and
: <math>g^{k\ell}\Gamma^i{}_{k\ell}=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{|g|}} \;\frac{\partial\left(\sqrt{|g|}\,g^{ik}\right)} {\partial x^k}</math>
where {{abs|''g''}} is the absolute value of the [[determinant]] of the matrix of scalar coefficients of the metric tensor <math>g_{ik}</math>.  These are useful when dealing with divergences and Laplacians (see below).

The [[covariant derivative]] of a [[vector field]] with components <math>v^i</math> is given by:
: <math>
v^i {}_{;j}=(\nabla_j v)^i=\frac{\partial v^i}{\partial x^j}+\Gamma^i{}_{jk}v^k
</math>
and similarly, the covariant derivative of a <math>(0,1)</math>-[[tensor field]] with components <math>v_i</math> is given by:
: <math>
v_{i;j}=(\nabla_j v)_i=\frac{\partial v_i}{\partial x^j}-\Gamma^k{}_{ij} v_k
</math>

For a <math>(2,0)</math>-[[tensor field]] with components <math>v^{ij}</math> this becomes
: <math>
v^{ij}{}_{;k}=\nabla_k v^{ij}=\frac{\partial v^{ij}}{\partial x^k} +\Gamma^i{}_{k\ell}v^{\ell j}+\Gamma^j{}_{k\ell}v^{i\ell}
</math>
and likewise for tensors with more indices.

The covariant derivative of a function (scalar) <math>\phi</math> is just its usual differential:
: <math>
\nabla_i \phi=\phi_{;i}=\phi_{,i}=\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x^i}
</math>

Because the [[Levi-Civita connection]] is metric-compatible, the covariant derivative of the metric vanishes,
: <math>
(\nabla_k g)_{ij} = 0, \quad (\nabla_k g)^{ij} = 0
</math>
as well as the covariant derivatives of the metric's determinant (and [[volume element]])
: <math>
\nabla_k \sqrt{|g|}=0
</math>
The [[geodesic]] <math>X(t)</math> starting at the origin with initial speed <math>v^i</math> has Taylor expansion in the chart:
: <math>
X(t)^i=tv^i-\frac{t^2}{2}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}v^jv^k+O(t^3)
</math>

A coordinates-free formula for the Levi-Civita connection (albeit being implicit) is the following:<ref>[[Manfredo do Carmo|M. P. Do Carmo]], Riemannian Geometry, p. 55</ref>
<math>
g(Z, \nabla_Y X)
=
\frac{1}{2}\Big(
              X( g(Y,Z))
              +
              Y( g(X,Z))
              -
              Z( g(X,Y))
              +
               g(Y,[Z, X])
              +
              g(X,[Z, Y])
              -
              g(Z, [X,Y])
\Big)
</math>

== Curvature tensors ==
=== Definitions ===
==== (3,1) [[Riemann curvature tensor]] ====
* <math>{R_{ijk}}^l=\frac{\partial\Gamma_{jk}^l}{\partial x^i}-\frac{\partial\Gamma_{ik}^l}{\partial x^j}+ \big(\Gamma_{jk}^p\Gamma_{ip}^l-\Gamma_{ik}^p\Gamma_{jp}^l\big)</math>
* <math>R(u,v)w=\nabla_u\nabla_vw-\nabla_v\nabla_uw-\nabla_{[u,v]}w</math>

==== (1,3) [[Riemann curvature tensor]] ====
* <math>{R^i_{jkl}}=\frac{\partial\Gamma_{lj}^i}{\partial x^k}-\frac{\partial\Gamma_{kj}^i}{\partial x^l}+ \big(\Gamma_{kp}^i\Gamma_{lj}^p-\Gamma_{lp}^i\Gamma_{kj}^p\big)</math>

==== [[Ricci curvature]] ====
* <math>R_{ik}={R_{ijk}}^j</math>
* <math>\operatorname{Ric}(v,w)=\operatorname{tr}(u\mapsto R(u,v)w)</math>

==== [[Scalar curvature]] ====
* <math>R= g^{ik}R_{ik}</math>
* <math>R=\operatorname{tr}_g\operatorname{Ric}</math>

==== Traceless Ricci tensor ====
* <math>Q_{ik}=R_{ik}-\frac{1}{n}Rg_{ik}</math>
* <math>Q(u,v)=\operatorname{Ric}(u,v)-\frac{1}{n}Rg(u,v)</math>

==== (4,0) Riemann curvature tensor ====
* <math>R_{ijkl}= {R_{ijk}}^pg_{pl}</math>
* <math>\operatorname{Rm}(u,v,w,x)=g\big(R(u,v)w,x\big)</math>

==== (4,0) [[Weyl tensor]] ====
* <math>W_{ijkl}=R_{ijkl}-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}R\big(g_{ik}g_{jl}-g_{il}g_{jk}\big)-\frac{1}{n-2}\big(Q_{ik}g_{jl}-Q_{jk}g_{il}-Q_{il}g_{jk}+Q_{jl}g_{ik}\big)</math>
* <math>W(u,v,w,x)=\operatorname{Rm}(u,v,w,x)-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}R\big(g(u,w)g(v,x)-g(u,x)g(v,w)\big)-\frac{1}{n-2}\big(Q(u,w)g(v,x)-Q(v,w)g(u,x)-Q(u,x)g(v,w)+Q(v,x)g(u,w)\big)</math>

==== [[Einstein tensor]] ====
* <math>G_{ik}=R_{ik}-\frac{1}{2}Rg_{ik}</math>
* <math>G(u,v)=\operatorname{Ric}(u,v)-\frac{1}{2}Rg(u,v)</math>

=== Identities ===

==== Basic symmetries ====
* <math>{R_{ijk}}^l=-{R_{jik}}^l</math>
* <math>R_{ijkl}=-R_{jikl}=-R_{ijlk}=R_{klij}</math>

The Weyl tensor has the same basic symmetries as the Riemann tensor, but its 'analogue' of the Ricci tensor is zero:
* <math>W_{ijkl}=-W_{jikl}=-W_{ijlk}=W_{klij}</math>
* <math> g^{il}W_{ijkl}=0</math>

The Ricci tensor, the Einstein tensor, and the traceless Ricci tensor are symmetric 2-tensors:
* <math>R_{jk}=R_{kj}</math>
* <math>G_{jk}=G_{kj}</math>
* <math>Q_{jk}=Q_{kj}</math>

==== First Bianchi identity ====
* <math>R_{ijkl}+R_{jkil}+R_{kijl}=0</math>
* <math>W_{ijkl}+W_{jkil}+W_{kijl}=0</math>

==== Second Bianchi identity ====
* <math>\nabla_pR_{ijkl}+\nabla_iR_{jpkl}+\nabla_jR_{pikl}=0</math>
* <math>(\nabla_u\operatorname{Rm})(v,w,x,y)+(\nabla_v\operatorname{Rm})(w,u,x,y)+(\nabla_w\operatorname{Rm})(u,v,x,y)=0</math>

==== Contracted second Bianchi identity ====
* <math>\nabla_jR_{pk}-\nabla_pR_{jk}=\nabla^lR_{jpkl}</math>
* <math>(\nabla_u\operatorname{Ric})(v,w)-(\nabla_v\operatorname{Ric})(u,w)=-\operatorname{tr}_g\big((x,y)\mapsto(\nabla_x\operatorname{Rm})(u,v,w,y)\big)</math>

==== Twice-contracted second Bianchi identity ====
* <math>g^{pq}\nabla_pR_{qk}=\frac{1}{2}\nabla_k R</math>
* <math>\operatorname{div}_g\operatorname{Ric}=\frac{1}{2}dR</math>

Equivalently:
* <math>g^{pq}\nabla_pG_{qk}=0</math>
* <math>\operatorname{div}_gG=0</math>

==== Ricci identity ====
If <math>X</math> is a vector field then
: <math>\nabla_i\nabla_jX^k-\nabla_j\nabla_iX^k=-{R_{ijp}}^kX^p,</math>
which is just the definition of the Riemann tensor. If <math>\omega</math> is a one-form then
: <math>\nabla_i\nabla_j\omega_k-\nabla_j\nabla_i\omega_k={R_{ijk}}^p\omega_p.</math>
More generally, if <math>T</math> is a (0,k)-tensor field then
: <math>\nabla_i\nabla_j T_{l_1\cdots l_k}-\nabla_j\nabla_iT_{l_1\cdots l_k}={R_{ijl_1}}^pT_{pl_2\cdots l_k}+\cdots+{R_{ijl_k}}^pT_{l_1\cdots l_{k-1}p}.</math>

==== Remarks ====
A classical result says that <math>W=0</math> [[if and only if]] <math>(M,g)</math> is locally conformally flat, i.e. if and only if <math>M</math> can be covered by smooth coordinate charts relative to which the metric tensor is of the form <math>g_{ij}=e^\varphi \delta_{ij}</math> for some function <math>\varphi</math> on the chart.

== Gradient, divergence, Laplace–Beltrami operator ==

The [[gradient#The gradient on manifolds|gradient]] of a function <math>\phi</math> is obtained by raising the index of the differential <math>\partial_i\phi dx^i</math>, whose components are given by:
: <math>\nabla^i \phi=\phi^{;i}=g^{ik}\phi_{;k}=g^{ik}\phi_{,k}=g^{ik}\partial_k \phi=g^{ik}\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x^k}
</math>

The [[divergence]] of a vector field with components <math>V^m</math> is
: <math>\nabla_m V^m = \frac{\partial V^m}{\partial x^m} + V^k \frac{\partial \log \sqrt{|g|}}{\partial x^k} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{|g|}} \frac{\partial (V^m\sqrt{|g|})}{\partial x^m}.</math>

The [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]] acting on a function <math>f</math> is given by the divergence of the gradient:
: <math>
\begin{align}
\Delta f &= \nabla_i \nabla^i f 
= \frac{1}{\sqrt{|g|}} \frac{\partial }{\partial x^j}\left(g^{jk}\sqrt{|g|}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x^k}\right) \\
 &=
g^{jk}\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^j \partial x^k} + \frac{\partial g^{jk}}{\partial x^j} \frac{\partial
f}{\partial x^k} + \frac12 g^{jk}g^{il}\frac{\partial g_{il}}{\partial x^j}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x^k}
= g^{jk}\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^j \partial x^k} - g^{jk}\Gamma^l{}_{jk}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x^l}
\end{align}
</math> 

The divergence of an [[antisymmetric tensor]] field of type <math>(2,0)</math> simplifies to 
: <math>\nabla_k A^{ik}= \frac{1}{\sqrt{|g|}} \frac{\partial (A^{ik}\sqrt{|g|})}{\partial x^k}.</math>

The Hessian of a map <math>\phi: M \rightarrow N </math> is given by
: <math> \left( \nabla \left( d \phi\right) \right) _{ij} ^\gamma= \frac{\partial ^2 \phi ^\gamma}{\partial x^i \partial x^j}- ^M \Gamma  ^k{}_{ij} \frac{\partial \phi ^\gamma}{\partial x^k} + ^N \Gamma ^{\gamma}{}_{\alpha \beta} \frac{\partial \phi ^\alpha}{\partial x^i}\frac{\partial \phi ^\beta}{\partial x^j}.</math>

== Kulkarni–Nomizu product ==

The [[Kulkarni–Nomizu product]] is an important tool for constructing new tensors from existing tensors on a Riemannian manifold.  Let <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> be symmetric covariant 2-tensors.  In coordinates,
: <math>A_{ij} = A_{ji} \qquad \qquad B_{ij} = B_{ji} </math>

Then we can multiply these in a sense to get a new covariant 4-tensor, which is often denoted <math> A {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} B</math>.  The defining formula is
: <math>\left(A {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} B\right)_{ijkl} = A_{ik}B_{jl} + A_{jl}B_{ik} - A_{il}B_{jk} - A_{jk}B_{il}</math>

Clearly, the product satisfies
: <math>A {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} B = B {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} A</math>

== In an inertial frame ==

An orthonormal [[inertial frame]] is a coordinate chart such that, at the origin, one has the relations <math>g_{ij}=\delta_{ij}</math> and <math>\Gamma^i{}_{jk}=0</math> (but these may not hold at other points in the frame). These coordinates are also called [[normal coordinates]].
In such a frame, the expression for several operators is simpler. Note that the formulae given below are valid ''at the origin of the frame only''.
: <math>R_{ik\ell m}=\frac{1}{2}\left(
\frac{\partial^2g_{im}}{\partial x^k \partial x^\ell} 
+ \frac{\partial^2g_{k\ell}}{\partial x^i \partial x^m}
- \frac{\partial^2g_{i\ell}}{\partial x^k \partial x^m}
- \frac{\partial^2g_{km}}{\partial x^i \partial x^\ell} \right)
</math>
: <math>R^\ell{}_{ijk}=
\frac{\partial}{\partial x^j} \Gamma^\ell{}_{ik}-\frac{\partial}{\partial x^k}\Gamma^\ell{}_{ij}
</math>

== Conformal change ==

Let <math>g</math> be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold <math>M</math>, and <math>\varphi</math> a smooth [[real-valued function]] on <math>M</math>.  Then
: <math>\tilde g = e^{2\varphi}g </math>
is also a Riemannian metric on <math>M</math>.  We say that <math>\tilde g</math> is (pointwise) conformal to <math>g</math>.  Evidently, conformality of metrics is an [[equivalence relation]].  Here are some formulas for conformal changes in tensors associated with the metric.  (Quantities marked with a tilde will be associated with <math>\tilde g</math>, while those unmarked with such will be associated with <math>g</math>.)

=== Levi-Civita connection ===
* <math>\widetilde{\Gamma}_{ij}^k=\Gamma_{ij}^k+\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x^i}\delta_j^k+\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x^j}\delta_i^k-\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x^l}g^{lk}g_{ij}</math>
* <math>\widetilde{\nabla}_XY=\nabla_XY+d\varphi(X)Y+d\varphi(Y)X-g(X,Y)\nabla \varphi</math>

=== (4,0) Riemann curvature tensor === 
* <math>\widetilde{R}_{ijkl}=e^{2\varphi}R_{ijkl}+e^{2\varphi}\big(g_{ik}T_{jl}+g_{jl}T_{ik}-g_{il}T_{jk}-g_{jk}T_{il}\big)</math> where <math>T_{ij}=\nabla_i\nabla_j\varphi-\nabla_i\varphi\nabla_j\varphi+\frac{1}{2}|d\varphi|^2g_{ij}</math>
Using the [[Kulkarni–Nomizu product]]:
* <math>\widetilde{\operatorname{Rm}} = e^{2\varphi}\operatorname{Rm} + e^{2\varphi}g {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} \left( \operatorname{Hess}\varphi - d\varphi\otimes d\varphi + \frac{1}{2}|d\varphi|^2g    \right)</math>

=== Ricci tensor ===
* <math>\widetilde{R}_{ij}=R_{ij}-(n-2)\big(\nabla_i\nabla_j\varphi-\nabla_i\varphi\nabla_j\varphi\big)-\big(\Delta\varphi+(n-2)|d\varphi|^2\big)g_{ij}</math>
* <math>\widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}=\operatorname{Ric}-(n-2)\big(\operatorname{Hess}\varphi-d\varphi\otimes d\varphi\big)-\big(\Delta\varphi+(n-2)|d\varphi|^2\big)g</math>

=== Scalar curvature === 
* <math>\widetilde{R}=e^{-2\varphi}R-2(n-1)e^{-2\varphi}\Delta\varphi-(n-2)(n-1)e^{-2\varphi}|d\varphi|^2</math>
* if <math>n\neq 2</math> this can be written <math>\tilde R = e^{-2\varphi}\left[R - \frac{4(n-1)}{(n-2)}e^{-(n-2)\varphi/2}\Delta\left( e^{(n-2)\varphi/2} \right) \right] </math>

=== Traceless Ricci tensor === 
* <math>\widetilde{R}_{ij}-\frac{1}{n}\widetilde{R}\widetilde{g}_{ij}=R_{ij}-\frac{1}{n}Rg_{ij}-(n-2)\big(\nabla_i\nabla_j\varphi-\nabla_i\varphi\nabla_j\varphi\big)+\frac{(n-2)}{n}\big(\Delta\varphi-|d\varphi|^2\big)g_{ij}</math>
* <math>\widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}-\frac{1}{n}\widetilde{R}\widetilde{g}=\operatorname{Ric}-\frac{1}{n}Rg-(n-2)\big(\operatorname{Hess}\varphi-d\varphi\otimes d\varphi\big)+\frac{(n-2)}{n}\big(\Delta\varphi-|d\varphi|^2\big)g</math>

=== (3,1) Weyl curvature === 
* <math>{\widetilde{W}_{ijk}}^l={W_{ijk}}^l</math>
* <math>\widetilde{W}(X,Y,Z)=W(X,Y,Z)</math> for any vector fields <math>X,Y,Z</math>

=== Volume form === 
* <math>\sqrt{\det \widetilde{g}}=e^{n\varphi}\sqrt{\det g}</math>
* <math>d\mu_{\widetilde{g}}=e^{n\varphi}\,d\mu_g</math>

=== Hodge operator on ''p''-forms === 
* <math>\widetilde{\ast}_{i_1\cdots i_{n-p}}^{j_1\cdots j_p}=e^{(n-2p)\varphi}\ast_{i_1\cdots i_{n-p}}^{j_1\cdots j_p}</math>
* <math>\widetilde{\ast}=e^{(n-2p)\varphi}\ast</math>

=== Codifferential on ''p''-forms === 
* <math>\widetilde{d^\ast}_{j_1\cdots j_{p-1}}^{i_1\cdots i_p}=e^{-2\varphi}(d^\ast)_{j_1\cdots j_{p-1}}^{i_1\cdots i_p}-(n-2p)e^{-2\varphi}\nabla^{i_1}\varphi\delta_{j_1}^{i_2}\cdots\delta_{j_{p-1}}^{i_p}</math>
* <math>\widetilde{d^\ast}=e^{-2\varphi}d^\ast-(n-2p)e^{-2\varphi}\iota_{\nabla\varphi}</math>

=== Laplacian on functions=== 
* <math>\widetilde{\Delta}\Phi=e^{-2\varphi}\Big(\Delta\Phi + (n-2)g(d\varphi,d\Phi)\Big)</math>

=== Hodge Laplacian on ''p''-forms === 
* <math>\widetilde{\Delta^d}\omega=e^{-2\varphi}\Big(\Delta^d\omega-(n-2p)d\circ \iota_{\nabla\varphi}\omega-(n-2p-2)\iota_{\nabla\varphi}\circ d\omega+2(n-2p)d\varphi\wedge\iota_{\nabla\varphi}\omega-2d\varphi\wedge d^\ast\omega\Big)</math>
The "geometer's" sign convention is used for the Hodge Laplacian here. In particular it has the opposite sign on functions as the usual Laplacian.

=== Second fundamental form of an immersion === 
Suppose <math>(M,g)</math> is Riemannian and <math>F:\Sigma\to(M,g)</math> is a twice-differentiable immersion. Recall that the [[second fundamental form]] is, for each <math>p\in M,</math> a symmetric [[bilinear map]] <math>h_p:T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma\to T_{F(p)}M,</math> which is valued in the <math>g_{F(p)}</math>-orthogonal [[linear subspace]] to <math>dF_p(T_p\Sigma)\subset T_{F(p)}M.</math> Then
* <math>\widetilde{h}(u,v)=h(u,v)-(\nabla\varphi)^\perp g(u,v)</math> for all <math>u,v\in T_pM</math>
Here <math>(\nabla\varphi)^\perp</math> denotes the <math>g_{F(p)}</math>-orthogonal projection of <math>\nabla\varphi\in T_{F(p)}M</math> onto the <math>g_{F(p)}</math>-orthogonal linear subspace to <math>dF_p(T_p\Sigma)\subset T_{F(p)}M.</math>

=== Mean curvature of an immersion ===
In the same setting as above (and suppose <math>\Sigma</math> has dimension <math>n</math>), recall that the [[mean curvature]] vector is for each <math>p\in\Sigma</math> an element <math>\textbf H_p\in T_{F(p)}M</math> defined as the <math>g</math>-trace of the second fundamental form. Then
* <math>\widetilde{\textbf H}=e^{-2\varphi}(\textbf H-n(\nabla\varphi)^\perp).</math>
Note that this transformation formula is for the mean curvature '''vector''', and the formula for the mean curvature <math>H</math> in the [[hypersurface]] case is
* <math>\widetilde{H}=e^{-\varphi}(H-n\langle\nabla\varphi,\eta\rangle)</math>
where <math>\eta</math> is a (local) normal vector field.

== Variation formulas ==
Let <math>M</math> be a smooth manifold and let <math>g_t</math> be a one-parameter family of Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian metrics. Suppose that it is a differentiable family in the sense that for any smooth coordinate chart, the derivatives <math>v_{ij}=\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\big((g_t)_{ij}\big)</math> exist and are themselves as differentiable as necessary for the following expressions to make sense. <math>v=\frac{\partial g}{\partial t} </math> is a one-parameter family of symmetric 2-tensor fields.
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\Gamma_{ij}^k=\frac{1}{2}g^{kp}\Big(\nabla_i v_{jp}+\nabla_jv_{ip}-\nabla_pv_{ij}\Big).</math>
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}R_{ijkl}=\frac{1}{2}\Big(\nabla_j\nabla_k v_{il}+\nabla_i\nabla_lv_{jk}-\nabla_i\nabla_kv_{jl}-\nabla_j\nabla_lv_{ik}\Big)+\frac{1}{2}{R_{ijk}}^pv_{pl}-\frac{1}{2}{R_{ijl}}^pv_{pk}</math>
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}R_{ik}=\frac{1}{2}\Big(\nabla^p\nabla_kv_{ip}+\nabla_i(\operatorname{div}v)_k-\nabla_i\nabla_k(\operatorname{tr}_gv)-\Delta v_{ik}\Big)+\frac{1}{2}R_i^pv_{pk}-\frac{1}{2} R_i{}^p{}_k{}^qv_{pq}</math>
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}R=\operatorname{div}_g\operatorname{div}_gv-\Delta(\operatorname{tr}_gv)-\langle v,\operatorname{Ric}\rangle_g</math>
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}d\mu_g=\frac{1}{2} g^{pq}v_{pq}\,d\mu_g</math>
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\nabla_i\nabla_j\Phi=\nabla_i\nabla_j\frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial t}-\frac{1}{2}g^{kp}\Big(\nabla_i v_{jp}+\nabla_jv_{ip}-\nabla_pv_{ij}\Big)\frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial x^k}</math>
* <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\Delta\Phi=-\langle v,\operatorname{Hess}\Phi\rangle_g-g\Big(\operatorname{div}v-\frac{1}{2}d(\operatorname{tr}_gv),d\Phi\Big)</math>

== Principal symbol ==
The variation formula computations above define the principal symbol of the mapping which sends a pseudo-Riemannian metric to its Riemann tensor, Ricci tensor, or scalar curvature.
* The principal symbol of the map <math>g\mapsto\operatorname{Rm}^g</math> assigns to each <math>\xi\in T_p^\ast M</math> a map from the space of symmetric (0,2)-tensors on <math>T_pM</math> to the space of (0,4)-tensors on <math>T_pM,</math> given by
*: <math>v\mapsto \frac{\xi_j\xi_kv_{il}+\xi_i\xi_lv_{jk}-\xi_i\xi_kv_{jl}-\xi_j\xi_lv_{ik}}{2} = -\frac12 (\xi \otimes \xi) {~\wedge\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\!\;\bigcirc~} v.</math>
* The principal symbol of the map <math>g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}^g</math> assigns to each <math>\xi\in T_p^\ast M</math> an endomorphism of the space of symmetric 2-tensors on <math>T_pM</math> given by
*: <math>v\mapsto v(\xi^\sharp,\cdot)\otimes\xi+\xi\otimes v(\xi^\sharp,\cdot)-(\operatorname{tr}_{g_p}v)\xi\otimes\xi-|\xi|_g^2 v.</math>
* The principal symbol of the map <math>g\mapsto R^g</math> assigns to each <math>\xi\in T_p^\ast M</math> an element of the [[dual space]] to the [[vector space]] of symmetric 2-tensors on <math>T_pM</math> by
*: <math>v\mapsto |\xi|_g^2\operatorname{tr}_gv+v(\xi^\sharp,\xi^\sharp).</math>
